note: v2: the tidal lock - half time, the jet in retrograde, an E7-carrier vocoder ("every corner comes sooner"), a snare rush rebuild
v4: the spiral tightens - bass and tide step back, the E1 bells, E5 (octave up), E4 and the hats/ghosts come forward one by one; the tide squeezes to a tremolo
v8: the storm opens into a progression - i VI III VII (Ebm Cb Gb Db), tide quarters then eighths, reese roots, offbeat stabs
v9: the storm gets a singer (voice-legato sings "every corner" on E1 in Eb minor at 33/41) and a way in (snare roll from 45, snare-tom fill at 48, kick out, landing)
v11: the storm in two steps - no Eb1 floor 17-24 (reese + octave-up double), riser and kick-out at 24, the floor drops at 25
v12: the singer doubled a fifth below (harmony -7, in key) at 53/61; half time 61-64 before the progression
v14: the head turns - Ebmaj7 | Cm9 | Abmaj9 | Bbsus4 -> Bb7 over t6s B-flat tail, the Bb7 resolving into the storm at 17
v15: an erhu answers the singer (A G F# E -> D, then E1 x2, A4 through the rush); her second statement a keyed third above (D mixolydian)
v20: the spiral turns down - Db(add9) / Cbmaj7 / Bb7sus4 from bar 101, home to Ebm at 113 with the singer
v21: the brass answers the singer (bars 35/43, falling to Eb) over a soft horn Ebm
v23: the collision lands - 808 Eb drop at bar 49, brass stabs on the offbeats (Ebm triad) around the singer
